tasks.short: Turn drawings, specifications and rates into a defensible cost estimate.

steps.what: Gather current drawings, specifications and scope instructions.
Read specifications and identify scope, exclusions and unresolved requirements.

loop.input: Versioned specifications and scope instructions from the estimate source pack.
loop.output: Draft scope register with source references, exclusions and unanswered questions.
loop.check: Validate document versions and references; estimator approves scope interpretation and missing requirements.
loop.stop: One extraction pass and one repair pass per document; unreadable or conflicting sections go to the estimator.
loop.why_not_simpler: Requirements appear in varied prose and cross-references; fixed fields cannot capture them reliably.

steps.what: Measure quantities and infer labour activities using the drawing measurement tool in {OTHER}.
Retrieve material prices, labour rates and relevant historical costs.
Calculate material, labour, equipment and overhead costs in the estimate workbook.
Assess productivity, uncertainty, exclusions and contingency; document the estimate basis.
Review assumptions and approve the estimate for bidding or pricing.

tasks.design: Configure versioned source packs in {DOCS} and an estimate template in {SPREADSHEET}, with rate retrieval from {ERP} through {DATA_PLATFORM}. A bounded extraction loop drafts the scope register with source references; the estimator checks scope, measures quantities and sets uncertainty allowances before commercial approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Drawing interpretation, inconsistent scope descriptions and disconnected rate sources made end-to-end automation unreliable.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing templates and rate interfaces handle calculation; faster coding makes the connecting work cheaper. Bounded text extraction can prepare a source-linked scope draft.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous drawings, buildability, site conditions and productivity assumptions still require expertise. Reliable geometric extraction is outside this initial build.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising an omitted activity or unrealistic production assumption before it becomes an expensive commitment.

ambition.what: An early design-options cost comparison using a common scope and rate basis.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling files and repeating calculations towards comparing design options and testing assumptions. Commercial approval rights stay unchanged.

reach.task: Translate estimate ranges into phased project budgets.
reach.learn: Budget phasing, contingency treatment and the distinction between cost estimates and spending authority.

evidence.claim: Versioned inputs, lookup tables and configured formulas can automate estimate assembly and arithmetic.
Scope extraction from specifications is plausible with bounded review; the digest contains no direct estimator deployment evidence.

assumptions: The reference workflow uses construction or engineered-product drawings; service estimates substitute activity volumes for drawing quantities.
The build covers one estimating template family and a limited set of source connections.
Approved rates have units, currencies, dates and applicability rules.
GDPR applies to identifiable labour data; EU AI Act obligations depend on actual use. Access time includes national consultation requirements where applicable.
unknowns: Whether drawings contain usable structured quantities or require manual measurement.
Which source identifies the latest authorised drawing revision.
Rate ownership, licensing restrictions and available interfaces.
Existing estimate software capabilities and commercial approval limits.
research_questions: Does existing software already provide rate lookup and estimate generation without custom code?
How accurately can scope extraction find exclusions and cross-references on representative specifications?
new_work: Review extracted scope against source passages.
Resolve stale rates, missing units and conflicting revisions.
Maintain estimate templates, rate mappings and regression examples.
Check generated packs for unsupported assumptions.

tasks.short: Agree estimate changes with technical specialists, customers and delivery partners.

steps.what: Compare the requested change with the approved estimate and prepare discussion points.

loop.input: Change request, approved estimate and estimate basis.
loop.output: Draft change brief with affected scope, source references and open questions.
loop.check: Check estimate version and line references; estimator validates scope interpretation.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unresolved scope remains explicitly open.
loop.why_not_simpler: Requests describe changes in prose and often imply dependencies absent from standard fields.

steps.what: Arrange the discussion and circulate the approved change brief.
Discuss technical alternatives, challenge assumptions and negotiate acceptable scope adjustments.
Document proposed agreements, unresolved issues and action owners.

loop.input: Estimator's discussion notes and proposed change terms.
loop.output: Draft change log separating proposed agreements, open issues and actions.
loop.check: Estimator checks each commitment, owner and date against notes; uncertain agreements remain unconfirmed.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; disputed wording returns to the participants.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text notes need interpretation to distinguish a proposal from an agreement.

steps.what: Recalculate affected estimate lines and show the cost difference.
Approve the revised estimate within delegated limits or escalate it.

tasks.design: Use {DOCS} and {WORKFLOW} to prepare a source-linked change brief, schedule discussion through {CALENDAR}, and draft a change log from written notes. Keep negotiation with people; configured calculations in {SPREADSHEET} produce a revised estimate for approval in {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: The core work depends on trust and technical negotiation, while preparation and documentation were scattered across files.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded drafting can organise change requests and notes. Existing scheduling, formula and approval features can handle the surrounding administration.
tasks.still_hard: Participants may disagree about scope, liability or what was agreed. A concise draft cannot settle those disputes.
tasks.human_edge: Discovering what each party can accept and recognising when apparent agreement conceals a costly misunderstanding.

ambition.what: A costed alternative-options brief before contentious change discussions.

tasks.altitude: The estimator spends less time preparing packs and recording decisions, leaving more preparation time for difficult conversations. Negotiation and approval limits stay unchanged.

reach.task: Assess the margin and cash implications of a proposed scope change.
reach.learn: Margin bridges, payment timing and delegated commercial authority.

evidence.claim: Configured scheduling, estimate formulas and approval routing can automate administration around a human discussion.
Bounded drafting from written notes can reduce documentation work, subject to checking commitments.

assumptions: Scheduling uses an approved participant list and approved brief; it makes no commercial commitment.
Recalculation follows estimator-confirmed quantities and rates; unresolved technical changes return to the estimator.
Approval follows delegated limits; contract amendments need their separate authorised approval.
The build uses written notes without introducing meeting recording.
GDPR and applicable EU AI Act requirements are assessed for the actual use; national consultation rules apply where relevant.
unknowns: Who can approve each class and value of change.
Whether external participants can access the shared change brief.
How approved estimate revisions are distinguished from contract variations.
Whether an existing workflow already covers change control.
research_questions: Can structured change forms remove enough ambiguity to avoid a drafting loop for routine requests?
Can reviewers reliably detect draft wording that overstates agreement?
new_work: Check draft briefs and change logs.
Resolve disputed commitments and unclear action owners.
Maintain participant access and approval limits.
Keep estimate revisions linked to the correct change decision.

tasks.short: Build a reusable historical cost base and select credible comparators for new estimates.

steps.what: Retrieve historical actual costs and project cost codes.
Find archived estimates, quantities and explanations of unusual costs.

loop.input: Archived estimates and project closeout notes for selected projects.
loop.output: Historical context register with quantities, scope differences and exceptional costs linked to sources.
loop.check: Validate project identifiers and source references; estimator checks quantities and exceptions before reuse.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per project; unsupported entries remain missing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Explanations of one-off costs and scope differences are embedded in varied narrative documents.

steps.what: Map cost codes and normalise units, currency and price dates.
Judge comparability and exclude misleading records or unsupported adjustments.
Publish the selected costs and their limitations for future estimates.

tasks.design: Load historical costs from {ERP} into {DATA_PLATFORM}, apply approved mappings and normalisation rules, and quarantine incomplete records. A bounded loop extracts context from {DOCS}; the estimator selects valid comparators and publishes them in a configured {WORKFLOW} records app with provenance and limitations.
tasks.previous_blocker: Historical records used inconsistent codes and lacked the context needed to distinguish repeatable costs from one-off events.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic data pipelines can handle mapping and normalisation. Faster coding lowers connector costs, while bounded extraction makes archived narrative context easier to recover.
tasks.still_hard: Missing quantities, changed accounting treatment and different delivery conditions can make apparently similar projects incomparable.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing when an attractive historical unit cost describes a fundamentally different job.

ambition.what: Give product development teams qualified cost ranges before detailed designs exist.

tasks.altitude: The estimator spends less time searching archives and repairing formats, and more time qualifying comparable work. They can accept or exclude comparators within an agreed method; budget approval rights stay unchanged.

reach.task: Define a reusable cost dataset with traceable measures.
reach.learn: Data grain, lineage, slowly changing mappings and validation rules.

reach.task: Reconcile historical project costs to posted accounting records.
reach.learn: Accruals, reversals, allocation changes and period closure.

evidence.claim: Cost collection, code mapping and normalisation are established deterministic data-processing patterns.
Historical comparability needs domain judgement even when records are structured.

assumptions: Initial scope covers one cost taxonomy and a bounded archive.
Normalisation uses approved exchange rates and price indices; missing values are not invented.
Published records retain original values, adjustment methods and source dates.
Labour data is aggregated where possible. GDPR applies to identifiable records; assess EU AI Act duties and national consultation rules if employee monitoring changes.
unknowns: Historical coverage, archive quality and rights to reuse supplier prices.
Availability of delivered quantities and final scope records.
Changes in cost codes, overhead allocation and accounting policies.
Whether comparator selection authority can be delegated to the estimator.
research_questions: Which fields most strongly determine comparability for the selected product or project family?
Can existing reporting exports supply the required data before building new interfaces?
new_work: Resolve quarantined records and missing context.
Maintain cost mappings, indices and source permissions.
Review ageing comparators and retire misleading benchmarks.
Monitor reconciliation totals and data refresh failures.

tasks.short: Compare actual costs with bids and judge whether delivery remains cost effective.

steps.what: Retrieve actual costs, commitments and delivery progress against the approved estimate.
Reconcile cost codes, accruals, commitments and scope changes in the monitoring workbook.
Calculate variance, unit costs and forecast scenarios against the bid baseline.
Investigate material variances and challenge progress and remaining-work assumptions.
Assess cost effectiveness and recommend delivery or forecast changes.
Approve corrective actions and the updated forecast within delegated limits.

tasks.design: Use existing variance reporting in {ERP} first, adding deterministic feeds from {PROCUREMENT} and {PROJECT} through {DATA_PLATFORM} where needed. Configure reconciliation checks and a {BI} dashboard that preserves the original bid and approved changes; estimators investigate exceptions and project managers approve forecasts and actions through {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Costs, commitments and progress arrived on different schedules and used different structures. Recurring reconciliation consumed time before useful analysis could start.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reporting and dashboard features already cover much of the calculation. Faster integration development makes cross-system refresh and exception routing more affordable.
tasks.still_hard: Actual costs lag delivery, progress can be overstated, and commitments can overlap invoices. Forecast quality still depends on credible remaining-work assumptions.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguishing timing differences from real cost deterioration and selecting an operational response that preserves value.

ambition.what: A weekly remaining-cost intervention decision for active projects with material exceptions.

tasks.altitude: The estimator reviews exceptions throughout the week instead of rebuilding a monthly workbook. They can initiate earlier intervention discussions; spending and forecast approval rights stay unchanged.

reach.task: Translate project cost changes into the rolling forecast.
reach.learn: Forecast drivers, uncertainty ranges and the separation of baseline, forecast and budget.

reach.task: Compare corrective actions by margin and cash impact.
reach.learn: Incremental costs, sunk costs and working-capital effects.

evidence.claim: Structured actual-versus-baseline calculations, exception rules and dashboards generally need deterministic technology.
Cost-to-complete forecasts require judgement about remaining work and cannot be inferred from spending alone.

assumptions: Project identifiers can be mapped across finance, purchasing and delivery records.
The baseline, approved changes and current forecast remain separate.
Forecast scenarios are provisional until approved; alerts do not authorise spending.
GDPR applies where costs identify individuals. EU AI Act duties depend on actual use; national consultation requirements need assessment if monitoring practices change.
unknowns: Whether existing reports already reconcile invoices, accruals and open commitments.
Reliability and frequency of progress updates.
Materiality thresholds, forecast ownership and escalation limits.
Whether labour costs can be supplied at an aggregated level.
research_questions: Which reconciliation failures most often distort the current cost position?
What refresh frequency would enable an operational decision before costs become unavoidable?
new_work: Resolve unmatched costs and commitment overlaps.
Maintain baseline mappings and materiality thresholds.
Check stale progress inputs and failed refreshes.
Review whether alerts produced useful interventions.

role.altitude: The role shifts towards scope interpretation, comparator quality, uncertainty and early cost interventions. Formal commercial and spending approval rights change only through explicit delegation.
reach: Budget analysts: turn qualified estimates into phased budgets and rolling forecasts.
Accountants: reconcile cost evidence and explain accounting effects.
Business intelligence analysts: maintain traceable cost measures and exception reporting.
Financial managers: assess margin and cash consequences of delivery alternatives.
skills_to_grow: Source checking and document version control
role.ambitious_version: Provide a cost-options advisory service from early design through delivery, using qualified historical evidence and current project costs to make uncertainty visible before commitments are made.
